title: Stack Subtraction Run
statement: Let $E,B$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{orc}$ be a Boolean oracle with four query types, let $x$ be a finite Boolean word, and let $b$ be a Boolean value. For any machine register state $\mathrm{st}$ whose eighteen register values are all at most $B$, the program has a finite run from the state for the phase-zero subtraction routine, with register values given by $\mathrm{st}$ and no answer, to the state for recovering the popped endpoint, with scratch register $Q$ set to zero, saved-endpoints register $SE$ set to $\max(\mathrm{st}.SE-\mathrm{st}.Q,0)$, and every other register unchanged; the answer remains absent. Every configuration before the final one satisfies the guard that the instruction meets its stated preconditions and every register value is at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: $\mathrm{orc}$ is a Boolean oracle with four query types
Every register value in $\mathrm{st}$ is at most $B$
replaced:
Let $E$, $B$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{orc}$ be a four-query Boolean oracle, let
$x$ be a bit string, and let $b$ be a Boolean value. For every register state
$\mathrm{st}$ whose eighteen register values are all at most $B$, the program has a
finite run from the phase-zero subtraction routine, with register vector given by
$\mathrm{st}$ and no answer, to the phase-zero move routine for recovering the popped
endpoint, with the scratch register $Q$ set to $0$, the endpoint stack $SE$ replaced by
$\max(SE-Q,0)$ using the original register values, and all other registers unchanged.
Every configuration before the final one satisfies the program’s guard requiring its
register values to be at most $B$ and its instruction to meet the program’s stated
preconditions.
